title: Role extraction reads from Keycloak's client-roles or realm-roles claim shape
description: Keycloak places roles on two claim families the operator selects between when configuring the client: `resource_access.<clientId>.roles` (per-client roles, the recommended default) and `realm_access.roles` (realm-wide roles). The realm record's `roleClaimShape` field declares which family this client uses (`client-roles` or `realm-roles`); the role adapter (TAC-1205) reads roles from that path on every verified token and populates the reduced Principal's `roles[]` array with the resulting string list. A token whose expected claim path is absent yields an empty `roles[]` (not a refusal); a project that wants stricter behaviour (a specific claim path must be present, or a specific role must be present, or the request is refused) authors a project-side authoriser above the reduced Principal and does not push that policy into the mechanism. The role adapter does not remap Keycloak role strings into project-defined role vocabulary; that remapping is a project-level concern and belongs on a project-authored ADR whose `related-reqs` cites this REQ.
rationale: Every project that uses Keycloak with role-based access must decide once whether its client is a per-client roles client or a realm-roles client; that decision is a Keycloak configuration and it lives on the realm record. Pushing role extraction to a single named adapter with a small surface keeps the project's handler code path free of Keycloak claim-shape knowledge and makes the role source observable in one place. Not remapping role strings inside the mechanism keeps the mechanism generic; a project that maps Keycloak roles onto its own project-role vocabulary does that once in an enrich-Principal hook the session-bridge invokes.
